claims.text: Monotherapy option for its anti-inflammatory activity
claims.quote: Bullous pemphigoid occasionally responds to the anti-inflammatory activity of certain drugs, such as the combination of tetracycline or minocycline and nicotinamide. Other treatment options include monotherapy with dapsone, sulfapyridine, or erythromycin.

claims.text: Can cause hemolytic anemia (risk highest after 1 month, higher with G6PD deficiency: test suspected patients first). Methemoglobinemia is common; hepatitis, agranulocytosis, dapsone syndrome (hepatitis and lymphadenopathy) and motor neuropathy are more serious
claims.quote: Dapsone can cause hemolytic anemia; risk is highest after 1 month of treatment and is increased in patients who have glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency. Patients suspected of having G6PD deficiency should be tested for this deficiency before being treated with dapsone. Methemoglobinemia is common; hepatitis, agranulocytosis, dapsone syndrome (hepatitis and lymphadenopathy), and a motor neuropathy are more serious complications.
